evidence: Created new product "QA Smart Blender 3000" (category Home Goods) via Admin > Add Product form with name, price, rating, image, affiliate link, tags, description, review, spec, featured toggle - "Product created successfully" toast shown and item appeared in list. Edited it (price 129->139) via Edit form - "Product updated successfully" toast, admin list reflected new price $139.
Category dropdown in Add/Edit Product form lists exactly three options: Tech Gadgets, Home Goods, Fitness. Nav bar and category pages also only expose these three verticals.

Edited existing product Sony WH-1000XM5 in Admin, added new tag "audiophile" to existing tags (headphones, wireless, noise-cancelling, premium). After saving, product detail page displayed all 5 tags including the newly added "audiophile".

Clicking a product card/title link (e.g., Sony WH-1000XM5 from /products list) navigated immediately (client-side route) to /product/sony-wh-1000xm5 detail page with full content rendered, no visible delay or lag.

Product detail page for Sony WH-1000XM5 fully displays: My Review section (full text), Key Specifications (Driver Size, Battery Life, Weight, Bluetooth, Noise Cancelling), price, rating, tags, and a "Buy Now" button linking to external retailer (https://example.com/sony-xm5).

Clicking "Buy Now" on the product detail page opened a new browser tab navigating to https://example.com/sony-xm5 (the external retailer link), while the original app tab remained on the product page.
/products page ("All Products") lists all 9 products, each showing category badge, name, price, rating, brief description, and a "Buy Now" purchase link.

On /products, selecting "Tech Gadgets" from the category filter combobox instantly updated the list to show exactly 3 products (Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra, Apple MacBook Pro 14", Sony WH-1000XM5), all labeled "Tech", and header changed to "3 products found".
Switching the category filter to "Tech Gadgets" updated the product grid and result count (9 -> 3) immediately/in-place without a page reload.

issue: Price range filter not enforced on results
actual: On /products, setting the Price Range 'Minimum' slider to $430 (confirmed via both the displayed '$430' label and the underlying aria-valuenow='430' on the slider element) did not exclude Sony WH-1000XM5 (priced $399, below the $430 minimum) from the result list. The count remained '8 products found' and Sony WH-1000XM5 was still visible/listed, both immediately after setting the slider and after pressing Tab (to commit/blur) and waiting 2 seconds. Category filter (Tech Gadgets -> 3 correct results) and Minimum Rating filter (4.5+ correctly excluded the 4.4-rated Philips Hue) worked correctly in isolation, but the Price Range filter criterion is not applied to the result set at all.
evidence: Price min slider=$430, list still shows Sony WH-1000XM5 ($399) among 8 results sorted ascending by price.

issue: Price range filter component does not filter results
actual: Sort by price (Low to High / High to Low) works correctly - verified ascending order: Sony ($399), Bowflex ($549), Theragun ($599), Breville ($699), Dyson ($749), Samsung ($1299), MacBook ($1999), Peloton ($2495). Minimum Rating filter also works correctly (4.5+ excludes the 4.4-rated Philips Hue Starter Kit). However, the Price Range minimum slider, part of the same filtering feature, does not actually filter the list: setting minimum to $430 left Sony WH-1000XM5 ($399) in the results. Since FT-10 requires filtering by price range to function, this is a partial failure of the required feature.
evidence: Price range slider set to $430 min; Sony WH-1000XM5 ($399) still present in filtered/sorted list.

Search box on /products correctly performs multi-dimensional matching: searching "Barista" (product name) returned 1 result (Breville Barista Express); searching "noise-cancelling" (a tag, not present in the product name) correctly returned Sony WH-1000XM5; description-text terms (e.g. names embedded in short description) also matched correctly. Confirms search covers name, tags, and description fields, updating result count/list in real time.

issue: Featured products not fully/correctly surfaced on homepage
actual: Marked "Bowflex SelectTech 552" as Featured via Admin edit form (toggled 'Featured on homepage' switch, Save Changes). The product correctly gained a 'Featured' badge in Admin list, on /products listing, and in the homepage 'Fitness' category row (4 products now show 'Featured' badge total: Sony, Peloton, Dyson, Bowflex). However, the homepage's dedicated 'Editor's Top Picks' section (the actual 'featured products' display) still only shows the original 3 items (Sony, Peloton, Dyson) and does NOT include the newly-featured Bowflex - it appears capped/hardcoded to 3 items rather than reflecting all currently-featured products. Additionally, clicking 'View all' on that section navigates to /products?featured=true, but that page ignores the featured=true query parameter entirely and shows all 9 products (including non-featured ones like MacBook, Theragun, Breville, Philips Hue) instead of filtering to only the 4 featured products.
evidence: Editor's Top Picks section shows 3 fixed products after adding a 4th featured item; /products?featured=true shows '9 products found' with unfeatured items included.

In Admin Edit Product form for Sony WH-1000XM5, clicked 'Add Spec' to create a new Label/Value pair, entered Label 'Charging Time' and Value '3 hours', then Save Changes. Product detail page's 'Key Specifications' section (reached via in-app navigation) now shows the newly created label 'Charging Time: 3 hours' alongside the original 5 specs.

In the same Admin edit session, renamed the existing spec label 'Weight' to 'Item Weight' (keeping value '250g') and saved. Product detail page correctly displays the updated label text 'Item Weight: 250g' in Key Specifications, confirming edits to existing labels persist and render correctly.

issue: No mechanism to categorize/group product labels
actual: Neither the product specification labels (Admin edit form 'Specifications' section) nor the tag-style labels (Tags filter panel on /products) offer any categorization/grouping capability. The Specifications editor is a flat list of Label/Value rows with no group/category field. The Tags filter panel on /products displays all ~34 tags as one flat alphabetical list mixed across Tech/Home/Fitness products, with no way to view or assign tags/labels by category/group. There is no UI anywhere in the app (Admin or public pages) to categorize existing labels into groups.
evidence: Admin Specifications editor: flat Label/Value rows only, no category field. /products Filters panel Tags section: single flat alphabetical list (ambiance, android, apple, ... wireless) with no grouping by category.

Spot-checked category/tag accuracy across all 10 products: Tech items (Sony WH-1000XM5, Apple MacBook Pro 14", Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra) correctly labeled 'Tech' with fitting tags (headphones/wireless, apple/laptop, android/smartphone/flagship); Home items (Dyson V15 Detect, Philips Hue Starter Kit, Breville Barista Express) correctly labeled 'Home' with fitting tags (vacuum/cordless, smart-home/lighting/automation, coffee/espresso/kitchen); Fitness items (Peloton Bike+, Theragun Pro, Bowflex SelectTech 552) correctly labeled 'Fitness' with fitting tags (cardio/cycling/smart-equipment/subscription, massage/recovery/therapy, dumbbells/weights/strength/home-gym). No mislabeling or category/tag mismatches observed across product cards, category pages, or detail pages.

Cross-checked core product data (name, category, price, rating, short description) across multiple views for several products (Sony WH-1000XM5, Peloton Bike+, Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra, Bowflex SelectTech 552): identical values appeared consistently on the homepage sections, /products list, category pages, and the individual product detail page, with no truncation of short description or full review text (e.g. Peloton's full review paragraph and Sony's Key Specifications rendered completely on the detail page) and no data loss between list-view and detail-view representations.
